arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/bsnake.sh
#!/bin/bash
stty -echo; echo -ne "\e[?25l"; H=$(tput lines); W=$(tput cols); ((H=H-4, W=W-2)); sh=0; sw=0; sR=(-1 0 1 0); sC=(0 1 0 -1); d=1; score=0; sr=$((H/2)); sc=$((W/2)); s="$sr,$sc"; for ((i=0;i<4;i++)); do ((sr-=sR[d], sc-=sC[d])); s="$s $sr,$sc"; done; fR=$((RANDOM%H)); fC=$((RANDOM%W)); clear
while :; do
  echo -ne "\e[H"
  for ((i=0;i<=W+1;i++)); do echo -ne "\e[1;${i}H\e[30;43m-\e[0m\e[$((H+2));${i}H\e[30;43m-\e[0m"; done
  for ((i=1;i<=H+2;i++)); do echo -ne "\e[${i};1H\e[30;43m|\e[0m\e[${i};$((W+2))H\e[30;43m|\e[0m"; done
  for ((r=0;r<H;r++)); do echo -ne "\e[$((r+2));2H\e[0K"; done
  echo -ne "\e[$((fR+2));$((fC+2))H\e[34;44m@\e[0m"; echo -e "\e[$((H+3));2H\e[31;43m Score: $score \e[0m"
  for p in $s; do IFS="," read -r r c <<< "$p"; echo -ne "\e[$((r+2));$((c+2))H\e[32;42mo\e[0m"; done
  read -s -n 1 -t 0.08 k
  case "$k" in [wWkK]) [ $d -ne 2 ] && d=0;; [dDlL]) [ $d -ne 3 ] && d=1;; [sSjJ]) [ $d -ne 0 ] && d=2;; [aAhH]) [ $d -ne 1 ] && d=3;; [qQ]) break;; esac
  tail_pos=$(echo $s | awk '{print $NF}'); IFS="," read -r tr tc <<< "$tail_pos"; echo -ne "\e[$((tr+2));$((tc+2))H "; head=$(echo $s | cut -d" " -f1); IFS="," read -r hr hc <<< "$head"; ((hr+=sR[d], hc+=sC[d]))
  if ((hr<0||hr>=H||hc<0||hc>=W)); then sh=1; fi
  for p in $s; do if [ "$hr,$hc" = "$p" ]; then sh=1; fi; done
  if [ $sh -eq 1 ]; then echo -e "\e[$((H/2+2));$((W/2-5))H\e[31;43m Oh, No! You 0xdead \e[0m"; sleep 1.5; break; fi
  s="$hr,$hc $s"
  if [ $hr -eq $fR ] && [ $hc -eq $fC ]; then
    ((score++)); sw=0
    while [ $sw -eq 0 ]; do fR=$((RANDOM%H)); fC=$((RANDOM%W)); sw=1; for p in $s; do if [ "$fR,$fC" = "$p" ]; then sw=0; fi; done; done
  else s=$(echo $s | sed "s/ [^ ]*$//"); fi
done
clear; echo -ne "\e[0m\e[?25h"; stty echo
EOF
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Starting snake game" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && bash /tmp/bsnake.sh && rm -f /tmp/bsnake.sh && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Generates and runs an interactive snake game that manages coordinate-specific rendering and restores the screen, text styles, and cursor state safely upon exit.
arguments.goal: Launch interactive terminal snake game with clean exit procedures

input: i want to measure my typing speed
how many words per minute i can type
test how fast i can type

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/btype.sh
#!/bin/bash
phrases=(
  "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
  "linux is a powerful open source operating system"
  "shell scripting automates boring tasks instantly"
  "cyber security protects data from malicious attacks"
  "artificial intelligence changes how we write code"
)
s="${phrases[$((RANDOM % ${#phrases[@]}))]}"
echo -e "═══ TYPING SPEED TEST ═══\r\n"
echo -e "Type this phrase as fast as you can:\r\n\e[1m$s\e[0m\r\n"
read -s -p "Press Enter to START..."
echo -e "\n\n═══ GO! ═══\r\n> $s\r"
t1=$(date +%s); read -re -p "> " input; t2=$(date +%s)
if [ "$input" = "$s" ]; then
  duration=$((t2 - t1))
  [ $duration -eq 0 ] && duration=1
  chars=${#s}
  wpm=$(( (chars * 60) / (5 * duration) ))
  echo -e "\r\nPerfect! 🎉\r\nTime taken: $duration seconds | Speed: $wpm WPM ⚡\r"
else
  echo -e "\r\nTypos detected! ⛔\r\nTry to be more accurate next time.\r"
fi
EOF
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Starting typing test" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && bash /tmp/btype.sh && rm -f /tmp/btype.sh && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Generates and runs a mini-game script to test your typing speed in Words Per Minute (WPM) directly inside the terminal without clearing screen history.
arguments.goal: Launch interactive terminal typing speed test
